criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the merge logic against the spec and the re-judge findings. Issues (2), (3), (4), (5 as direct indexing), (7), and the dead-branch cleanup appear addressed in lines 96-103, 143-152, and 195-198. But issue (1) is still broken: lines 129 and 141 do not implement 'same provider OR same independence_group count as one vote' correctly, and lines 202-206 introduce a new path-only `--reveal-shadow` gate that can reveal the current shadow verdict after an ack on an older artifact state.

Most quorum scenarios are covered, including seat-missing, invalid rows, evidence mismatch, and shadow-seat suppression. However, a required auto-pass condition from spec §2 row 1 is still missing: line 147 can auto-pass without any canary-freshness check, and lines 27-28 explicitly admit that this part is deferred. That leaves a load-bearing piece of the spec unimplemented.

I checked for repo/house-facing conventions visible from this file: placement under `.claude/evals/` is consistent, legacy `claude`/`gemini` blocks are preserved at lines 175-177, and the quorum record only adds fields rather than removing the expected ones. I did not see a write-path or naming convention violation in this file, but I could not fully verify broader repo conventions from this artifact alone, so I would not award 1.0.

The implementation stays fairly lean: no hardcoded secrets, no obvious resurrected tombstoned tooling, and no unnecessary platform-building beyond the quorum logic itself. The problems I found are logic/integrity defects rather than over-engineering or speculative-surface anti-patterns, so this still passes with normal reviewer scrutiny rather than a top score.

There are some good diagnostic choices here: unknown seat ids fail loudly with exit 2 (lines 195-198), integrity reasons are broken out explicitly, and the canary gap is at least documented in comments. But lines 62-63 silently skip malformed/latest partial seat rows and can reuse an older record, which is exactly the kind of opaque failure mode the rubric says to send back. The user-facing contract in lines 40-42 therefore overstates the safety of the ingestion path.

defects.quote: return s_.get("independence_group") or s_.get("provider") or sid      # provider OR group: spec §2
defects.spec_ref: Spec §2 ("Seats with the same provider or the same `independence_group` count as one vote.")
defects.description: Issue (1) is not actually fixed. This chooses `independence_group` first and only falls back to `provider`, so two seats from the same provider but different groups are still treated as independent.

defects.spec_ref: Spec §2 ("Seats with the same provider or the same `independence_group` count as one vote.")
defects.description: Same-group/provider voting seats are not collapsed into one effective vote; they are only converted into an escalation reason. That contradicts the spec's 'count as one vote' rule and can over-escalate cases that should follow the one-voting-seat path instead.

defects.spec_ref: Spec §2 row 1 (auto-pass requires "canaries fresh"); Spec §11 build step 8
defects.description: Issue (9) remains unresolved. The auto-pass branch has no canary-freshness check and no runtime reason when freshness is unknown, so a required gate from the spec is still absent.

defects.quote: r.get("record_type") == "quorum" and r.get("artifact") == a.artifact and r.get("alex_ack")
defects.spec_ref: Spec §1 (shadow output is hidden until after ack so the label stays uncontaminated)
defects.description: `--reveal-shadow` is unlocked by any acked quorum row for the same artifact path, not for the current artifact state/hash. A previously acked version of the file can therefore reveal the current shadow verdict before this version is acked.
Malformed JSON lines are silently skipped. If the newest seat entry is corrupted, the merger can fall back to an older row without surfacing `seat_invalid` or another loud integrity signal.

defects.quote: if r.get("record_type") != "quorum" and r.get("artifact") == artifact and r.get("verdict") in ("pass", "flag"):
defects.description: `last_row()` does not actually use the last row for the artifact; it uses the last parseable row that already has a final verdict. A latest partial row with no `verdict` is silently ignored, so the partial-row fix only covers some malformed rows and the CLI contract at lines 40-42 overstates what happens.

checks_performed: Compared the resolution matrix in `merge()` against spec §2 and the nine re-judge issues, including integrity-vs-quality reasons, unanimous FLAG handling, and PASS auto-resolution.
Traced vote-independence handling through `group_of()`, `groups`, and `verdicts` to see whether same-provider / same-independence-group seats are actually collapsed to one effective vote.

Checked the evidence-integrity paths: `evidence_unverified`, bundle-hash checks, evidence parity, flat-ceiling handling, and whether those signals remove vote and/or escalation power as the spec says.
Reviewed CLI and logging behavior in `main()`: unknown seat ids, `--reveal-shadow` enforcement, quorum log writing, legacy compatibility fields, and additive metadata.
Inspected seat-row ingestion in `last_row()` / `valid_row()` for partial-row, malformed-row, and stale-row behavior to see whether the earlier crash fix now degrades loudly instead of silently.
